info.title: Apache APISIX Admin API
info.description:
The **Apache APISIX Admin API** is a RESTful interface for managing all APISIX gateway resources — routes, upstreams, services, consumers, SSL certificates, plugins, and more.

APISIX Admin API allows you to dynamically configure the API gateway without restarts. All changes take effect immediately.

Unless API key authentication is explicitly disabled with `deployment.admin.admin_key_required: false`, endpoints require an **API key**. Pass a key configured under `deployment.admin.admin_key` in APISIX's `config.yaml` using the `X-API-KEY` request header.

The default Admin API listens on `http://127.0.0.1:9180`. You can customize the host and port in `config.yaml` under `deployment.admin.admin_listen`.

To learn how to configure and operate APISIX, see [Get Started](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/getting-started/).

tags.name: Routes
tags.description:
A **Route** defines how client requests are matched and forwarded to upstream services. Routes are the most fundamental resource in APISIX — every incoming request is evaluated against configured routes.

A route must include at least a **URI pattern** and one of: an inline `upstream`, an `upstream_id`, a `service_id`, or `plugins`.

**Key Features**
- Match by URI, host, HTTP method, headers, query parameters, and custom expressions
- Attach plugins for authentication, rate limiting, transformation, and more
- Support WebSocket proxying and gRPC transcoding
- Priority-based routing when multiple routes match

To learn how to configure routes, see [Routes](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/routes).

tags.name: Upstreams
tags.description:
An **Upstream** is a virtual host abstraction over a pool of backend service nodes. It defines how APISIX distributes traffic to your backend servers.

**Load Balancing Algorithms**
- `roundrobin` — Weighted round-robin (default)
- `chash` — Consistent hashing for session affinity
- `ewma` — Latency-based selection (exponentially weighted moving average)
- `least_conn` — Fewest active connections

**Health Checks**
Upstreams support **active** and **passive** health checks to automatically remove unhealthy nodes from the load balancing pool.

To learn how to configure upstreams, see [Upstreams](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/upstreams).

tags.name: Services
tags.description:
A **Service** is a reusable abstraction that groups an upstream and a set of plugins. Multiple routes can reference the same service, reducing configuration duplication.

When a route references a service via `service_id`, the service's upstream and plugins are merged with the route's own configuration. Route-level settings take precedence.

To learn how to configure services, see [Services](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/services).

tags.name: Consumers
tags.description:
A **Consumer** represents an API user, application, or host that consumes your APIs. Consumers are typically used with authentication plugins (e.g., `key-auth`, `jwt-auth`) to identify callers and apply per-consumer rate limits or access controls.

Each consumer is uniquely identified by a `username` and can belong to a consumer group.

To learn how to configure consumers, see [Consumers](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/consumers).

tags.name: Consumer Groups
tags.description:
A **Consumer Group** allows you to define shared plugin configurations that apply to multiple consumers. Instead of duplicating plugin settings across consumers, assign them to a group.

Consumers reference a group via the `group_id` field. Group-level plugins are merged with consumer-level plugins, with consumer-level taking precedence.

To learn how to configure consumer groups, see [Consumer Groups](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/consumer-groups).

tags.name: Credentials
tags.description:
A **Credential** stores authentication configuration associated with a consumer. Each credential holds exactly one authentication plugin (e.g., `key-auth`, `basic-auth`, `jwt-auth`).

Credentials are sub-resources of consumers. A consumer can have multiple credentials, each for a different authentication method.

To learn how to configure consumer credentials, see [Credentials](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/credentials).

tags.name: Plugins
tags.description:
**Plugins** extend APISIX's core functionality with middleware capabilities such as authentication, traffic control, observability, and request/response transformation.

Use these endpoints to query available plugins and their JSON schemas, or to hot-reload plugins without restarting APISIX.

Plugins are attached to routes, services, consumers, or global rules via the `plugins` object.

See [Plugin Hub](https://docs.api7.ai/hub) for the full list of available plugins.

tags.name: Plugin Configs
tags.description:
A **Plugin Config** is a reusable set of plugin configurations that can be shared across multiple routes. Instead of duplicating plugin settings in each route, create a plugin config and reference it via `plugin_config_id`.

Route-level plugins are merged with plugin config plugins, with route-level taking precedence.

To learn how to configure reusable plugin configurations, see [Plugin Configs](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/plugin-configs).

tags.name: Plugin Metadata
tags.description:
**Plugin Metadata** configures shared settings that apply to all instances of a specific plugin across the entire APISIX cluster. This is useful for plugins that need global configuration, such as log format templates.

For example, setting metadata for `http-logger` will affect every route that uses `http-logger`.

To learn how to configure plugin metadata, see [Plugin Metadata](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/plugin-metadata).

tags.name: Global Rules
tags.description:
A Global Rule applies plugins to incoming requests independently of route and service configuration. For HTTP requests, global and local plugins are interleaved by phase: global `rewrite`, local `rewrite`, global `access`, then local `access`. Plugin priority applies within each phase and scope.

To learn how to configure global rules, see [Plugin Global Rules](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/plugin-global-rules).

tags.name: Stream Routes
tags.description:
A **Stream Route** defines TCP/UDP layer (L4) proxying rules. Unlike HTTP routes, stream routes operate at the transport layer and can proxy raw TCP and UDP connections.

Stream routes match traffic by `remote_addr`, `server_addr`, `server_port`, or `sni` (for TLS connections).

**Note:** Stream mode must be enabled in `config.yaml` (`apisix.proxy_mode: stream` or `http&stream`) before creating stream routes.

To learn how to configure stream routes, see [Stream Routes](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/stream-routes).

tags.name: SSL Certificates
tags.description:
The **SSL** resource manages TLS certificates for HTTPS termination and mTLS authentication.

**Certificate Types**
- `server` — Server certificate for HTTPS termination (matched by SNI)
- `client` — Client certificate for mTLS with upstream services

APISIX dynamically selects the correct certificate based on the SNI (Server Name Indication) in the TLS handshake. Certificates can be rotated without restart.

To learn how to configure TLS certificates, see [SSL Certificates](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/ssl-certificates).

tags.name: Secrets
tags.description:
The **Secret** resource integrates APISIX with external secret managers (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) for dynamic secret retrieval at runtime.

Once configured, you can reference secrets in plugin configurations using the URI format: `$secret://vault/my-secret/key`.

To learn how to configure secret managers, see [Secrets](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/key-concepts/secrets).

tags.name: Protos
tags.description:
The **Proto** resource stores Protocol Buffer (protobuf) `.proto` file content used by the `grpc-transcode` plugin to convert between HTTP/JSON and gRPC.

Upload your `.proto` definitions here, then reference them by ID in the `grpc-transcode` plugin configuration.

To learn how to configure gRPC transcoding, see [gRPC Transcode](https://docs.api7.ai/hub/grpc-transcode).

post.description:
Validates a declarative APISIX configuration when the deployment uses either the `etcd` or `yaml` configuration provider. The endpoint accepts JSON and YAML request bodies up to 1.5 MiB and uses the normal Admin API authentication.

Validation covers known resource arrays, numeric `*_conf_version` fields, duplicate resource identifiers, resource JSON Schemas, and plugin `check_schema` functions. All detected errors are returned together. Cross-resource existence is not checked, so a reference such as an `upstream_id` can pass even when the referenced resource is absent. The operation does not persist or apply any configuration.

ConfigValidationRoute.description:
Route configuration. A route matches incoming requests by URI, host, methods, and other conditions, then forwards them to an upstream.

A route must have at least a `uri` (or `uris`) and one of: `upstream`, `upstream_id`, `service_id`, or `plugins`.

Declarative route configuration. The optional `modifiedIndex` controls resource-level change detection with the YAML configuration provider.

desc.description: Description of what this route does.

update_time.description: Unix timestamp of last update. Read-only.

uri.description: URI path pattern to match. Supports exact match (`/api/v1/users`) and prefix match (`/api/*`). Mutually exclusive with `uris`.

uris.description: Multiple URI patterns. Mutually exclusive with `uri`.

host.description: Single hostname to match against the request's `Host` header. Supports wildcard prefix (`*.example.com`). Mutually exclusive with `hosts`.

hosts.description: Multiple hostnames to match. Mutually exclusive with `host`.

methods.description: HTTP methods allowed on this route. If empty or not set, all methods are allowed.

remote_addr.description: Single client IP address or CIDR range to match. Mutually exclusive with `remote_addrs`.

remote_addrs.description: Multiple client IP addresses or CIDR ranges to match. Mutually exclusive with `remote_addr`.

priority.description: Route priority. When multiple routes match the same request, the one with the highest priority wins.

vars.description: Custom matching conditions using [APISIX expressions](https://docs.api7.ai/apisix/reference/router-options). Each condition is an array of `[variable, operator, value]`.

filter_func.description: Custom Lua function for advanced request matching. Must start with `function`.

plugin_config_id.description: Reference to a Plugin Config resource. Cannot be used together with `script`.

upstream_id.description: Reference to an existing Upstream resource.

service_id.description: Reference to an existing Service resource.

enable_websocket.description: Enable WebSocket proxying on this route.

script.description: Lua script for plugin orchestration. Cannot be used together with `plugins` or `plugin_config_id`.

script_id.description: Script ID (used internally by APISIX Dashboard).

modifiedIndex.description: Optional resource version used for change detection by the YAML configuration provider.

update_time.description: Unix timestamp of last update. Read-only.

upstream_id.description: Reference to an existing Upstream resource.

enable_websocket.description: Enable WebSocket proxying for routes using this service.

modifiedIndex.description: Optional resource version used for change detection by the YAML configuration provider.

ConfigValidationUpstream.description:
Upstream configuration defining backend service nodes and load balancing behavior.

An upstream must specify either `nodes` (static list) or `service_name` + `discovery_type` (service discovery).

Declarative upstream configuration. The optional `modifiedIndex` controls resource-level change detection with the YAML configuration provider.

create_time.description: Unix timestamp when the upstream was created. Read-only, set automatically.

update_time.description: Unix timestamp when the upstream was last updated. Read-only, set automatically.

retries.description: Number of retry attempts when a request to the upstream fails.

retry_timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds for retry attempts. `0` disables the retry timeout.

x-enumDescriptions.ewma: Latency-based load balancing using an exponentially weighted moving average.

hash_on.description: What to hash on when `type` is `chash`.

x-enumDescriptions.vars: Hash on an NGINX variable specified by `key`.
x-enumDescriptions.header: Hash on a request header specified by `key`.
x-enumDescriptions.cookie: Hash on a cookie value specified by `key`.
x-enumDescriptions.consumer: Hash on the authenticated consumer name.
x-enumDescriptions.vars_combinations: Hash on a combination of variables.

key.description: The hash key used when `type` is `chash`. Required when `hash_on` is `header`, `cookie`, `vars`, or `vars_combinations`. Not needed when `hash_on` is `consumer`.

scheme.description: Protocol for communicating with upstream nodes.

x-enumDescriptions.wss: Frame-aware WebSocket proxying over TLS; uses the shared CA trust store, not `tls.ca_certs`.

pass_host.description: How to set the `Host` header when proxying to the upstream.

upstream_host.description: Custom `Host` header value. Only effective when `pass_host` is `rewrite`.

discovery_type.description: Service discovery type (e.g., `dns`, `consul`, `nacos`, `eureka`). Required when using service discovery instead of static `nodes`.

namespace_id.description: Namespace ID for Nacos service discovery.

service_name.description: Service name for service discovery. Required when `discovery_type` is set.

modifiedIndex.description: Optional resource version used for change detection by the YAML configuration provider.

key.description: PEM-encoded private key. Can also be a secret reference (`$secret://...`). **Not returned in GET responses for security.**

ConfigValidationStreamRoute.description:
Stream Route for TCP/UDP (L4) proxying. Matches transport-layer connections by client IP, server address/port, or SNI.

Declarative stream route configuration. The optional `modifiedIndex` controls resource-level change detection with the YAML configuration provider.

update_time.description: Unix timestamp of last update. Read-only.

remote_addr.description: Client IP address or CIDR range to match.

sni.description: SNI hostname to match. Supports wildcard hostnames. Mutually exclusive with `snis`.

modifiedIndex.description: Optional resource version used for change detection by the YAML configuration provider.

snis.description: Alternative SNI hostnames to match, including wildcard hostnames. Mutually exclusive with `sni`.

tls_passthrough.description: On a listener configured with both `tls` and `tls_passthrough`, `true` forwards encrypted TLS bytes to the upstream; `false` terminates TLS at APISIX. Ignored on dedicated listeners. Passthrough requires a TCP upstream, not scheme `tls`.

ConfigValidationGlobalRule.description:
Global Rule configuration. Global plugins apply independently of locally bound plugins. For HTTP requests, execution is interleaved by phase: global `rewrite`, local `rewrite`, global `access`, then local `access`. Priorities order plugins within each phase and scope, and an early response skips handlers scheduled later.

Declarative global rule configuration. The optional `modifiedIndex` controls resource-level change detection with the YAML configuration provider.

UpstreamWarmUp.description: Gradually increases the effective weight of newly observed nodes. Only supported for HTTP upstreams using `roundrobin` and a single node priority; ignored by stream routes and rejected in inline `traffic-split` upstreams. The initial node set is already warmed. Each gateway instance tracks ramps independently. This changes traffic distribution, not the total request rate.

slow_start_time_seconds.description: Seconds for a new node to reach its configured weight.

min_weight_percent.description: Minimum percentage of the configured node weight. Effective positive weights are rounded down but never below 1.

interval.description: Seconds between weight refreshes. Cannot exceed `slow_start_time_seconds`.

aggression.description: Ramp shape: 1 is linear, above 1 is faster initially, and below 1 is slower initially.

startup_grace_period_seconds.description: Seconds after the gateway starts during which newly observed nodes are treated as already warmed.
